statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail moves from 14 to 16 because the recovery the previous assessment described as extending has since stalled and partially faded, while the cross-asset backdrop tightened further. NQ futures were verified at 29,196.25, down 252.50 points or 0.86%, inside a 29,044.25 to 29,508.25 session range; cash NAS100 at 29,149.80 has slipped from the 29,250.41 session high it set in the previous hour. The decisive observation is that the 29,038.22 cash low, set at the opening auction, has still not been retested after more than two cash hours. Retracements in both directions are occurring, which is mean reversion functioning rather than failing. Against that, Brent at $106.93 is up 5.65% at fresh session highs, the ten-year Treasury yield at 4.93% is up about 8 basis points to its highest since October 2023, the two-year at 4.55% is up about 10 basis points, and VIX at 17.65 is up 7.2% though still below its 18.05 session high. Semiconductors are broadly weaker while several megacaps are higher, which is dispersion rather than the aligned amplifier stack a no-retracement path requires.
recommendation: Tail at 16 maps the policy state to EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution false under the fixed repository mapping. The danger window stays drawn narrowly around 12:30 to 13:30 UTC on 11 September, covering the August consumer price index and the first hour of post-release price discovery, which remains the next scheduled point at which a no-retracement structure could plausibly form. Conditional tail reaches 22 in the 12:00 UTC slot tomorrow and 20 in the hour after; those are the only two forward slots mapped to the watch band. A secondary conditional peak of 19 sits in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots today, where U.S. cash trading closes and Oracle's fiscal Q1 2027 results are scheduled into materially thinner futures liquidity; that peak stays inside the low band because thin-book reactions are normally discontinuous gaps rather than sustained one-way paths, and because Oracle is NYSE-listed so its transmission to the Nasdaq-100 runs through software and AI-capex sentiment rather than index weight. Stress rises to 85 and remains extreme: August producer prices at 0.4% on the month and 5.4% on the year, crude at fresh highs on Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea escalation, an ECB that raised its three key rates today with effect from 16 September, and a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September into markets now pricing roughly a 70% chance of a hike are all unresolved. Stress at that level describes the environment and does not on its own move the mapped state past the blocking threshold.
headline: NQ fades to 29,196.25 as the intraday recovery stalls short of the session high, but the 29,038.22 low holds untested while Brent pushes to $106.93 and the ten-year yield reaches 4.93%; tail rises from 14 to 16.
body:
The hour changed the tone without changing the structure. An hour ago cash NAS100 was making progressively higher session highs and NQ sat roughly 190 points above its low. Now NQ is at 29,196.25, down 0.86%, and cash NAS100 at 29,149.80 has given back part of the advance after peaking at 29,250.41. That is a stalled recovery, not a reversal: the 29,038.22 opening-auction low is still untested, and price has moved in both directions within a roughly 210-point cash band for several hours. Under the framework used here, tail measures the probability of a price path that denies meaningful mean reversion for long enough to overwhelm a reverse or grid approach. A band that is being traded in both directions is the opposite of that path, which is why tail stays deep in the low band at 16 rather than moving toward the blocking threshold.

What did deteriorate is the cross-asset backdrop. Brent at $106.93 is up 5.65% and at fresh session highs, higher than an hour ago, on intensified shipping attacks in the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. The ten-year Treasury yield at 4.93% is up about 8 basis points to its highest level since October 2023 and the two-year at 4.55% is up about 10 basis points, after August producer prices rose 0.4% on the month and 5.4% on the year. Interest-rate futures now imply roughly a 70% chance of a Federal Reserve hike on 16 September, up from about 61% yesterday. VIX at 17.65 is up 7.2% but has not exceeded its 18.05 session high, which is the signature of a market repricing rather than one dislocating. That combination is why stress moves up to 85 while tail moves only two points.

The internals argue against alignment. Semiconductors are broadly weaker in the latest available cross-sectional context while several megacaps are higher, so the index decline is being driven by one complex rather than by everything moving together. An aligned amplifier stack, with yields, oil, volatility, semiconductors, megacaps and breadth all pushing the same way alongside shallow or failed retracements, is the configuration that would justify a materially higher reading. It is not present. Confidence stays at 88 because current levels, ranges, yields, crude, volatility and the release calendar were all verified directly this hour.

The forward path keeps the tail floor overnight and concentrates conditional risk at three scheduled checkpoints: the crude settlement and power hour into the U.S. close today, Oracle's after-the-bell results into thin liquidity this evening, and the August consumer price index at 12:30 UTC tomorrow. Only the two slots covering that release and the cash open after it are mapped to the watch band. Everything else in the forward window remains in the low band, and every structural claim about hours after the current one is stated as an assumption or an invalidation rather than as an observation.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 16:00 UTC on 9 September to 15:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at tail 13 with a mixed read, drifts down to a 12 to 8 band across the U.S. close and the overnight session, and holds a narrow 9 to 11 range through the Asian and early European hours. The turn sits in the final five slots: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC as the mode switched to trend-down on the pre-release grind, tail 20 at 12:00 UTC with the mapped state at WATCH around the producer price release, a window high of tail 24 at 13:00 UTC covering the U.S. cash open and the opening decline, then 17 at 14:00 UTC and 14 at 15:00 UTC as the index recovered off its opening low. The current reading of 16 is a modest step back up from that trough, and the whole 24-hour path stayed inside the low and watch bands throughout.
outlookSummary: The forward window opens with the intraday recovery stalled but the session low intact, and closes in the U.S. mid-morning after a consumer price release. Conditional tail starts at 16 in the current 16:00 UTC hour, holds 16 into the following hour, then ticks to 17 across the crude settlement and the power hour. It reaches its afternoon peak of 19 in the 20:00 and 21:00 UTC slots, which contain the U.S. cash close and Oracle's scheduled fiscal Q1 2027 results into thin futures liquidity, before decaying through 16 and 13 into the late evening. Overnight the path settles to an 11 floor across the Asian session, then climbs gradually through 12, 12, 13, 13, 14, 14 and 15 as European trade and pre-release positioning build, reaching 22 in the 12:00 UTC slot that contains the August consumer price index and 20 in the hour that contains the U.S. cash open, before easing to 17 and 15. Those two release slots are the only ones mapped to the watch band; the rest of the window stays in the low band. Confidence declines from 88 to 80 across the window because the evidence supporting the later hours is scheduled-calendar knowledge rather than observed price path.
